question: Does FAA guidance say which failsafe mode a drone should be programmed with for a lost link?
stop_reason: claims still failing after the revision limit

intake.focus: lost link failsafe mode FAA guidance
intake.reason: FAA guidance on failsafe behavior for lost control link

brief.short_answer: FAA guidance: AC 107-2A says to try to reestablish the control link after loss and, if unsuccessful, start emergency/contingency procedures for loss of control link; it also notes regaining VLOS when practicable but without a specified interruption time. Manuals: DJI Matrice 210 V1 states Failsafe RTH activates after more than three seconds of signal loss; RTH can be canceled to regain control; it plans a return route and will descend/land if within 65 feet of the Home Point. Incident reports: Autel EVO Max 4N reports (unverified) describe loss of control after takeoff, platform flying away, failed Return To Home, and failure to locate the UAS.

claims.text: AC 107-2A states that when a link loss occurs, try to reestablish control link connection with the small unmanned aircraft; if connection cannot be reestablished, start emergency or contingency procedures for loss of control link.
claims.quote: Try to reestablish control link connection with the small unmanned aircraft. If connection cannot be reestablished, start emergency or contingency procedures for loss of control link.

claims.text: AC 107-2A indicates that if the remote PIC cannot regain VLOS, the remote PIC or person manipulating the controls should follow pre-determined procedures for the loss of VLOS.
claims.quote: If the remote PIC cannot regain VLOS, the remote PIC or person manipulating the controls should follow pre-determined procedures for the loss of VLOS.
conditions: cannot regain visual line of sight (VLOS)

claims.text: AC 107-2A notes that the remote PIC should regain VLOS as soon as practicable, with no specific permissible interruption time specified for VLOS; actions depend on the capability of the UAS.
claims.quote: regain VLOS as soon as practicable.
conditions: remote PIC may briefly lose sight of the aircraft
no specific time interval for VLOS interruption exists

claims.text: AC 107-2A describes transfer of operational control between certificated remote pilots only if both are capable of maintaining VLOS of the small UAS without loss of control.
claims.quote: both capable of maintaining Visual Line of Sight (VLOS) of the small unmanned aircraft without loss of control (LOC).
conditions: two or more certificated remote pilots transferring control
VLOS without LOC must be maintained

C001.rationale: The cited passage states to try to reestablish the control link and, if that fails, to start emergency/contingency procedures for loss of control link.

C002.rationale: The cited passage says if the remote PIC cannot regain VLOS, they should follow pre-determined procedures for the loss of VLOS.

C003.rationale: The cited passage requires regaining VLOS as soon as practicable and states no specific permissible interruption time for VLOS; it notes actions depend on UAS capabilities.

C004.rationale: The cited passages describe transfer of control between certificated remote pilots only if both can maintain VLOS without LOC.

C006.rationale: Passage states Failsafe RTH is automatically activated if the remote controller signal is lost for more than three seconds, given Home Point recorded and compass functioning normally.

C007.rationale: Passage states the user may cancel Failsafe RTH to regain control when connection is reestablished.

C008.rationale: Passage states the aircraft will plan its return route and retrace its original flight route home as part of Failsafe RTH.

C009.rationale: Passage states aircraft cannot return to Home Point when GPS signal is weak or unavailable.

C010.rationale: Passage states aircraft will automatically descend and land if RTH is triggered within 65 feet (20 meters) of Home Point.
